item.text: {"verdicts":[{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0016-E001","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0016-E002","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0016-E003","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"In a 2023 submission to the UN Human Rights Committee, the International Commission of Jurists identified ongoing concerns in Egypt involving torture and other ill-treatment, enforced disappearance, abusive pre-trial detention and poor treatment of persons deprived of liberty, fair-trial rights, and judicial independence.","notes":["The excerpt says “poor treatment of persons deprived of their liberty,” not specifically “poor detention conditions.”"]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0016-E004","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0016-E005","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0016-E006","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"Amnesty International’s retrospective account states that activist Alaa Abdel Fattah was arrested on 29 September 2019 amid a widespread crackdown, sentenced in December 2021 by an Emergency State Security Court to five years in prison on charges of spreading false news, and was later described as being arbitrarily detained beyond the sentence’s stated end date.","notes":["The excerpt does not specifically establish that he remained arbitrarily detained during 2023."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0016-E007","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]}]}
